title: Observability fingerprinting & replay-safe watermarking for on-prem collectors
creator: Sana Mukherjee
description:
Problem: Dedicated and private on-prem collectors receive replays and duplicate telemetry during network flaps and customer-side retries. Existing tenant scoping approaches are brittle for air-gapped and VPC deployments where we cannot rely on global ingest coordination. Goal: Add a lightweight, local-friendly mechanism that (1) produces a per-collector 'signal fingerprint' for incoming request batches, (2) attaches a replay-safe watermark to persisted envelopes, and (3) exposes translation hints to Console dashboards so SREs can confidently attribute latency/error spikes to a tenant or to collector replays. This should work without cross-tenant centralized coordination and must preserve privacy boundaries for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters.

Proposed approach: implement a three-part feature set: (A) Signal fingerprint: compute a compact, non-identifying fingerprint (hmac-truncated) over request-level routing headers + short KV-cache ids to allow local dedup heuristics. (B) Replay-safe watermarking: generate monotonic ingest watermarks scoped to a collector instance that survive restarts via a write-ahead marker file and optional cloud-backed checkpoint when available. Watermarks are used by downstream pipelines to suppress duplicate traces/logs during a replay window. (C) Dashboard translation layer: add a Console transformation that uses fingerprint-to-tenant binding hints to show whether a spike is "collector replays" vs "true tenant traffic" and expose a Replay Suppression metric on latency/error dashboards.

Constraints & privacy: fingerprints must be one-way, not contain raw tenant identifiers, and be revocable. Watermark storage must tolerate collectors running in air-gapped mode (local disk fallback) and be hardened to clock skew. Backpressure and storage IO must be budgeted for low-end on-prem boxes.

Success metrics: reduce duplicate-trace re-ingest rate by >= 80% during common replay scenarios; dashboards should flag replay suppression for > 95% of automated replays in integration tests; negligible added latency (<1ms median) to collect path.
acceptance_criteria: Collector computes and logs a non-reversible signal fingerprint per request batch
Collector persists a monotonic watermark that survives controlled restarts and is used by ingest pipeline to suppress duplicates
Console exposes a Replay Suppression toggle and shows fingerprint-derived hints on latency/error dashboards
Integration test suite simulates network replay with deterministic duplicates and demonstrates >=80% deduplication
Configuration flags for collectors: replay_window_ms, fingerprint_salt, watermark_persistence_path
Security review sign-off documenting privacy guarantees and KMS usage for optional remote checkpoints
updates: 2026-02-12 — Initial design doc posted. Author: Sana Mukherjee. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/onprem-observability-fingerprint-spec (internal). Asked infra for recommended local persistence patterns for air-gapped boxes.

2026-02-18 — Spike completed by Ethan Ross: validated a lightweight HMAC-128 truncated fingerprint has acceptable collision bounds on our request distributions. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/2345 (draft).

2026-02-25 — Design review with Product & Privacy (Marcus Chen, Priya Natarajan). Decided to avoid carrying tenant IDs inside fingerprints; will adopt a revocable-salt approach and document rotation procedures.
2026-03-03 — Hooked watermark persistence into collector start/stop flow. Found edge case with clock skew causing non-monotonic watermarks after container restore; added monotonic counter fallback.

2026-03-08 — Integration harness updated to inject replay scenarios (flaky TCP + client-side retry storm). Early runs show ~72% deduplication; next actions: tighten matching heuristics and add optional lightweight payload signature.
2026-03-10 — Security review requested. Submitted security checklist and threat-model note for fingerprints and checkpointing. Link: https://security.redwood.local/reviews/OBS-105432 (internal).
